newsitem.title: UK: LDN FREIGHT - PANAMAX DECLINE SEES BFI BELOW 1,400.
newsitem.headline: LDN FREIGHT - PANAMAX DECLINE SEES BFI BELOW 1,400.

text.p: The rapid descent of the panamax market took the Baltic Freight index (BFI) under 1,400 for the first time since February 5, brokers said.
On Wednesday the BFI was fixed down 19 points at 1,392.
Freight conditions were weak generally but the downward trend was nowhere more pronounced than in the panamax grain trades from the U.S. Gulf and in the north Pacific.
Some brokers thought a bounce must soon come and that it was too early for the start of a traditional summer of weak demand.
GRAIN - U.S. Gulf/Japan rates fell again, as seen by Cho Yang fixing of the Navios Mariner.
The Navios Mariner was taken for 54,000 tonnes heavy grain for May 3/15 at $22.50 no combo (some reports put the rate at $23.65), down 35 cents to one dollar from previous fixtings.
Brokers reported that owners were willing to repeat $22.50 for first half May but charterers were now quoting only $22.00.
North Pacific grain rates were also softer, with the Joyous Age booked by Pan Ocean for 54,000 tonnes heavy grain Nopac/Japan for early May at $14.25 no combo.
There was talk circulating the market that the same charterers took the Keoyang-relet Samjohn Captain at similar levels, possibly less.
Another relet, the 1982-built Camarina, was even thought to have been fixed at under $14.00 no combo in this trade.

Equally serious for owners were reports that Halla had fixed the Klaveness-relet Northern Venture 68,400 dwt, which sailed from Muroran two days ago, delivery Nopac for a trip to Taiwan with grain at a substantially weaker $10,500 daily plus $175,000 ballast bonus, but failed on subjects.

A steadier rate was obtained by Flavia 65,242 dwt from Pan Ocean delivery Taiwan April 17 for a grain trip via Australia to Egypt with redelivery Red Sea at close to $10,750 daily, option redelivery Mediterranean at about $7,000/$7,250 daily.

Other incomplete reports of grain fixtures included Pateras to Continental for 54,000 tonnes heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Japan for April 25/30 (possibly at $23.00 no combo), and Finagrain with Ludolf Oldendorff 64,442 dwt from U.S. Gulf to Jeddah and Dammam (possibly for around $1.2m lumpsum).
Toepfer fixed Maritime Vision for about 30,000 tonnes 55' U.S. Gulf/Continent for April 18/25 at a lumpsum equivalent of an economical $16.00.
Cargill booked 15,000 tonnes sunflower seeds river Plate/Manzanillo on private terms, but otherwise the handy sector was quiet.

New grain house enquiries included Cargill's 50/55,000 tonnes heavy grain up river Plate and Necochea or Bahia Blanca/Egyptian Mediterranean for April 21/30, Halla 50,000 tonnes heavy grain up river Plate completing Brazil/Indonesia or Malaysia May 5/14, Dreyfus 54,000 tonnes grain Brazil/Taiwan for prompt up to early May, and Pan Ocean for a panamax delivery U.S. Gulf May 20/30 trip Far East.

Smaller size enquiries included Toepfer for 30,000 tonnes heavy grain Mississippi/Jakarta May 1/15, Delta Bakeries 35,000 tonnes wheat U.S. Gulf/Alexandria May 7/14, Garnac 8,000 tonnes corn, 3,000 sbm, 10,000 wheat U.S. Gulf/Rio Haina April 25/30.
MINERALS - Coal business was reportedly booked by Bocimar with Anne for 100,000 tonnes Baltimore/Sines for May 2/11 at $5.50.
Full details were missing of NYK's fixture of Anangel Progress 69,406 dwt Queensland/Chile, and Carboex with Bona tonnage for about 60,000/10 Davant/Tarragona for May 1/15.
Kleimar was understood to have taken a Marshal-class vessel for about 100,000/10 iron ore Nouadhibou/Antwerp at about $4.00/4.50.
Short period fixtures of about three to five months of panamaxes were concluded basis prompt delivery Far East.
This business was done by Pan Ocean with Joyous Land 69,200 dwt at $11,000 daily (including sulphur), and by Shinwa on subjects with Merchant Pioneer 69,700 dwt at $11,100 daily (excludiung sulphur).
At 1505 the BIFFEX futures stood nine to 32 points easier than Tuesday's close. Most active May saw 126 lots, with the last trade done at 1,335, down 30 points. Total volume ammounted to 255 lots.
-- Stephen Grainger +44 171 542 8074.
